rows.Note: Element kanji 火 (Hi). Release romaji/遁 kanji are standard series terminology (not quoted verbatim for the basics in the fetched page).
Non-elemental; based on spiritual energy / imagination. Underlies some genjutsu-type and form-creating abilities. Outside the five-nature cycle.
Non-elemental; based on physical energy / vitality. Underlies life-giving / body-related techniques. Shares romaji 'Yōton' with Lava Release (熔遁/溶遁) but different kanji.
Uses Yin and Yang simultaneously. Jutsu not researched (not an elemental combination).

rows.Japanese (romaji): Fire > Wind > Lightning > Earth > Water > Fire  (each nature beats the next one in the loop and loses to the one before it)

Combined natures can inherit weaknesses (anime: Pakura's Scorch Release is weak to Water, Shippūden ep. 285). Kekkei tōta users are said (anime ep. 267) to have an affinity for all three natures they combine.

rows.Notable users: Hashirama Senju (only natural user); Yamato, Danzō, Madara, Obito, White Zetsu, Orochimaru (via Hashirama cells); Moegi (Boruto); Asura Ōtsutsuki (anime-only); Katasuke & Momoshiki (Boruto movie novelisation); Ten-Tails/God Tree

rows.Description: Basic wood control: angular timber grows from the ground, the arms or the palms.
rows.Verification: Single source (Pixiv only); romaji romanised from kanji by researcher (not quoted from source)

rows.Romaji: Mokuton Bunshin / Moku Bunshin no Jutsu
rows.Description: The user's cells become plant matter to make a durable clone. It can fight on its own, merge with trees to scout, or ride along as a seed and act as a tracker; it soaks up damage instead of popping like a normal clone.
rows.Users: Hashirama Senju; Madara Uchiha (Yamato also per Pixiv's seed-tracking note; not separately verified)

rows.Kanji: 木遁・多重木遁分身の術

rows.Verification: Single source (Pixiv only); romaji romanised from kanji by researcher (not quoted from source)

rows.Users: Obito Uchiha; Ten-Tails (through Obito and Madara's link to it)

rows.Canon status: Manga + anime; Sha no Sho p.305

rows.Verification: Verified; romaji romanised from kanji by researcher (not quoted from source)

rows.Verification: Verified; romaji romanised from kanji by researcher (not quoted from source)

rows.Description: The user's arm becomes trees that grow fast and branch out, catching enemies or skewering them with stake-like tips.
rows.Verification: Verified; romaji romanised from kanji by researcher (not quoted from source)

rows.Description: The arm turns into branches that wrap the target like rope and pin it in place. Strong enough to hold a giant squid.

rows.Canon status: Manga (ch. 293); Sha no Sho p.308; card game
rows.Verification: Verified; romaji romanised from kanji by researcher (not quoted from source)

rows.Detail: Narutopedia's Category pages (e.g. Category:Wood_Release), the MediaWiki API, BreezeWiki/antifandom mirrors and other-language editions were inaccessible during research, and many individual jutsu pages failed to load. Jutsu lists were rebuilt from nature pages, individual jutsu/character/episode pages, Pixiv Encyclopedia (Japanese), a Naruto Boutique blog and search results. Lists may therefore be incomplete, especially for game-only jutsu.
All descriptions are paraphrases taken from the research notes, not quotations.
Romaji, kanji or users are left blank where the notes did not provide them; nothing was filled in from memory.

Mud Release is Novel-only (Akatsuki Hiden: Evil Flowers in Full Bloom), not anime-only. Blaze Release is a Mangekyō Sharingan ability (Sasuke, Kagutsuchi); its Fire + Lightning pairing comes only from the mobile game Naruto Mobile. Guren is confirmed as the Crystal Release user.

Ice Sword Technique: Pixiv credits Rahyō, Narutopedia credits Kahyō. Lava Rubber Spheres: Narutopedia says manga, Pixiv says novel-original. Planet-Branding Blast: page content showed the name 'Muddy Stream Wave'. (Boil Release: corrected — Kokuō is the Five-Tails; its jinchūriki is Han, not Utakata.)
Description and users come from a page that was actually fetched and read (jutsu, character, episode or nature page). Qualifiers in brackets note partial issues.
Details come from one secondary source only (e.g. Pixiv Encyclopedia or the Naruto Boutique blog) without a matching Narutopedia page being read.
A page with this title exists (seen in search results or a list) but its content was not retrieved; description/users/status are unverified.
A lead from researcher memory or an unconfirmed URL; treat as a lead, not a fact.
Romaji was transliterated by the researcher from the kanji given in the source, not quoted from the source.
A described use of the nature that has no official jutsu name.
Manga = Kishimoto's manga or databooks; Anime-only = filler; Movie; Novel (Hiden/Shinden); Game; Boruto. 'Name from game' means the feat appears in canon but its name comes from a game.
